desk.headline: Latest results: Q2 revenue up 23% to RMB14.5bn (reported 18 Aug); 2026 parcel outlook cut to 6–10%; Q3 results due 17 Nov
results: The 17 November filing is a Hong Kong buyback return, not results: ZTO bought 2,309 ADSs on 12 Nov and 17.3m shares (2.26%) under its June mandate so far. Q3 results are due on 17 Nov (US time).
In Q2 (reported 18 Aug) parcel volume grew 6.5% to 10.5bn, while revenue rose 23% to RMB14.5bn on a 15.5% higher price per parcel, helped by return-parcel business for large accounts.
Adjusted net income rose 50% to RMB3.09bn (RMB3.79 per ADS); gross margin improved to 25.7%.
Operating cash flow was RMB4.6bn and capital spending RMB952m.
No interim dividend: buybacks of $740m this year already met the target of returning at least 50% of prior-year adjusted profit.

guidance.summary: ZTO cut its 2026 parcel volume forecast to 40.8–42.4bn (6–10% growth) from 42.37–43.52bn (10–13%), citing slower industry growth.

points: The CEO stressed service quality and said volume grew 2.3 points faster than the industry.
Retail and return parcels are growing faster than standard e-commerce parcels and lifting margins.
Combined sorting and transport cost per parcel fell 2 cents, helped by automation and route planning.
The CFO called the market subdued and pointed to government moves against price wars.
call.source: Management comments in the Q2 2026 press release (19 Aug 2026); no reliable call coverage found

watch: Q3 results on 17 Nov: whether the 6–10% volume range holds.
Whether higher prices per parcel last as industry price competition is curbed.
Pace of buybacks under the $1.5bn programme ($1.36bn left at end-June).
